entry.focal: The vanishing point at the end of the first straight leg, framed by symmetric pairs of wall lanterns.
entry.next_visible: A dead-end wall with a lantern. There is no orange hint of the turn.

reveal.focal: The chamber opening framing the orange glass wall, with white lantern posts in front. This is the right idea.
reveal.next_visible: Yes, the chamber is clearly next.

concept.focal: A straight leg with paired lanterns, symmetric. It reads as a service corridor.
concept.next_visible: No orange is visible beyond the bend.

strip.focal: Legs 1 and 2 have even mirrored lantern pairs. From frame 5 the orange chamber appears and grows. This is a good reveal at the end.

fixes.detail: side: both plus spacing [4,5] gives mirrored pairs at identical stations (a runway). Stagger the sides (alternate) with spacing [4,7], and make fade_toward visible: the last 3-4 niches before the bend should be at ≤50% intensity.
The tunnel is three straight legs with hard kinks; plan 36 is a smooth S-curve. Fillet the corners with r ≥ 12 m so the walls hide what is ahead and the glow spills round the curve.
rock_cluster produced only 1 object (density 0.06, band [0,0.4]). Raise the density to 0.15 on the outside of the two bends so the walls are not bare boxes there.
The bench at (50.4,47.4) is not visible in any frame. Shift it so it faces down the last leg toward the glow.

top_change: Curve the tunnel and stagger and fade its lanterns so the orange chamber glow is hinted from the first bend instead of appearing only on the last leg.
plausibility: None serious. The headroom (3.5 m) and the 4x3 m neck are fine.
